title: Lime rolls out its in-house 'Lime Vision' camera AI that chirps at sidewalk riders to half of its 7,000-scooter Seattle fleet by 1 June 2026
summary: Seattle Times (20 Mar 2026): Lime Vision uses cameras and AI to detect sidewalk riding and emit repeating audible alerts; 3,500 scooters by 1 June 2026, whole fleet by year-end; no outcome data yet.
account: Nicholas Deshais of The Seattle Times reported on 20 Mar 2026 (syndicated by The Spokesman-Review, which is the copy read here) that Lime would fit 'Lime Vision', a system of cameras and AI software developed in-house to detect sidewalk riding and emit audible alerts that repeat until the scooter leaves the sidewalk or the trip ends, to about 3,500 vehicles, half its Seattle fleet, by 1 June 2026 and to the whole fleet by year's end, with new and retrofitted scooters arriving from mid-April. Parker Dawson, Lime's regional government relations lead, said the technology had been tested in Seattle in recent months, that Seattle would get it before any other city, and that it coaches riders rather than slowing the scooter; he would not say why the scooters do not slow down on sidewalks as they do under geofencing at Seattle Center. Jon Scholes of the Downtown Seattle Association called sidewalk riding a safety issue. Lime shares data with a Seattle Department of Transportation dashboard. The article gives no sidewalk-riding or complaint figures before or after deployment; the date given is the publication date.
purpose: Lime Vision was built to detect sidewalk riding and deter it through audible alerts.
system: Lime Vision (on-scooter cameras with AI sidewalk-riding detection and audible alerts)
taxonomy_note: Launch report only: one independent news report with named sources, no evaluation data; the city's role is limited to a data dashboard. A later SDOT blog post (14 May 2026) on bike and scooter share safety was found in a site search but its text was not read.

ratings.reason: No outcome is documented; the article describes a rollout.
No outcome for Lime or SDOT is documented.

ai_role.statement: The article describes the intended function; no detection counts, accuracy or behavioral results are reported, and Lime declined to share many details.
